Low-rank adaptation (LoRA; Hu et al., 2022 ) is a standard parameter-efficient alternative to full fine-tuning: it scales to large models, is easy to compose with existing training stacks, and is widely treated as the default way to specialize a pretrained language model on a new task or domain Schulman and Thinking Machines Lab (2025) ; Biderman et al. (2024) . A common piece of practitioner wisdom is that increasing LoRA rank increases adapter capacity: a larger r r enlarges the low-rank update subspace and can support richer task-specific changes Raschka (2023) ; Schulman and Thinking Machines Lab (2025) ; Liu et al. (2024b) . This intuition is appealing and often borne out at moderate ranks, yet it rests on an implicit assumption that is rarely checked: that the adapter actually uses the subspace it is given.

In parallel, fine-tuning, whether full-rank or parameter-efficient, faces a persistent learning–forgetting tension. Fitting a target distribution can improve task metrics while erasing competence on broad pretraining domains, and heterogeneous or sequential training regimes exacerbate the trade-off Kirkpatrick et al. (2017) ; Hu et al. (2022) . LoRA is not exempt: in mixed-domain and continual-learning settings, adapters often lag full fine-tuning on target-task fit while still paying a substantial retention cost on pretraining proxies Biderman et al. (2024) ; Shuttleworth et al. (2024) . Prior work has proposed many remedies, such as stronger parameterizations Kopiczko et al. (2024) , norm constraints Wang et al. (2025) , spectral initialization Meng et al. (2025) , and deliberately tiny adapters Morris et al. (2026) . However, these approaches frequently reallocate the trade-off rather than improve it: methods that fit the fine-tuning mixture well can forget aggressively, whereas methods that limit forgetting often underfit the new data (Figure 2 ).

We primarily experimented with Qwen2.5 Yang et al. (2025) : 0.5B base, 3B-instruct, and 7B-instruct. For single-task fine-tuning settings, we used math reasoning (GSM8K Cobbe et al. (2021) ), low-resource language instruction fine-tuning (Aya Hausa Singh et al. (2024) ), and machine translation (WMT19 cs-en Barrault et al. (2019) ) datasets. We also experimented in a supervised mixed-domain fine-tuning setting that proxies continual learning – we fine-tune with assistant-only SFT on a fixed 10 6 10^{6} -token budget over a shuffled mixture of three domains: GSM8K ( 45 % 45\% ), WMT19 Czech–English ( 10 % 10\% ), and Aya Hausa instruction-following ( 45 % 45\% ). To measure forgetting in this continual learning setting, we report held-out perplexities on fixed reference slices from the Wiki and StarCoder components of OLMo-Mix-1124 OLMo et al. (2024) (pretraining-distribution proxies, denoted Wiki PPL and StarCoder PPL) and on GSM8K and WMT19 Czech–English (in-mixture math and translation retention, respectively). Baselines include standard LoRA, dense down-projection fine-tuning, and the following adapter variants: PiSSA Meng et al. (2025) , LoRA-XS Bałazy et al. (2025) , TinyLoRA Morris et al. (2026) , SVF Sun et al. (2022) , VeRA Kopiczko et al. (2024) , and unpenalized NB-LoRA Wang et al. (2025) . Unless noted, adapters target all MLP down_proj layers at LoRA rank r = 896 r{=}896 ; dense down-projection fine-tuning updates the same module subset. We typically experiment with λ ∈ { 0 , 0.01 , 0.1 , 1.0 } \lambda\in\{0,0.01,0.1,1.0\} . For full details about our setup, baselines, and datasets, refer to Appendix F . Below, we report representative slices of our empirical comparison to summarize our major findings and takeaways. Additional comparisons appear in Appendix

Unless a table caption states otherwise, all numbers are taken from the terminal training state of a completed run; we do not reload an in-run best-validation checkpoint. Early stopping is disabled. Periodic evals run every 100 100 optimizer steps; perplexity and forgetting probes below are the values logged at the last eval before the run hits its token or epoch budget. Train PPL is exp ⁡ ( H ) \exp(H) where H H is an exponential moving average ( β = 0.99 \beta{=}0.99 ) of the assistant-only training loss; it is a smoothed training-loss proxy, not held-out validation perplexity. Wiki PPL and StarCoder PPL are reference-probe perplexities on fixed OLMo-Mix-1124 slices, using the plain-text supervision protocol and batch limits specified above. In the mixed-domain setting we additionally log in-mixture retention probes on held-out GSM8K and WMT19 Czech–English validation text; Appendix Table 5 reports both in-mixture probes. eRank is the Roy–Vetterli effective rank of the accumulated adapter update Δ ​ W \Delta W , averaged over all targeted down_proj modules, taken from the last logged rank diagnostic. This is distinct from the Rényi-2 surrogate used in the objective. Dense down-projection fine-tuning baselines select hyperparameters via a separate sweep (Section F.1 ), but reported metrics still refer to the terminal state of the selected run. Post-hoc spectral analyses (intruder dimensions, subspace alignment, singular-direction mixing) use measurements from the final saved checkpoint.

LoRA is not exempt: in mixed-domain and continual-learning settings, adapters often lag full fine-tuning on target-task fit while still paying a substantial retention cost on pretraining proxies Biderman et al. (2024) ; Shuttleworth et al. (2024) . Prior work has proposed many remedies, such as stronger parameterizations Kopiczko et al. (2024) , norm constraints Wang et al. (2025) , spectral initialization Meng et al. (2025) , and deliberately tiny adapters Morris et al. (2026) . However, these approaches frequently reallocate the trade-off rather than improve it: methods that fit the fine-tuning mixture well can forget aggressively, whereas methods that limit forgetting often underfit the new data (Figure 2 ).

We primarily experimented with Qwen2.5 Yang et al. (2025) : 0.5B base, 3B-instruct, and 7B-instruct. For single-task fine-tuning settings, we used math reasoning (GSM8K Cobbe et al. (2021) ), low-resource language instruction fine-tuning (Aya Hausa Singh et al. (2024) ), and machine translation (WMT19 cs-en Barrault et al. (2019) ) datasets. We also experimented in a supervised mixed-domain fine-tuning setting that proxies continual learning – we fine-tune with assistant-only SFT on a fixed 10 6 10^{6} -token budget over a shuffled mixture of three domains: GSM8K ( 45 % 45\% ), WMT19 Czech–English ( 10 % 10\% ), and Aya Hausa instruction-following ( 45 % 45\% ). To measure forgetting in this continual learning setting, we report held-out perplexities on fixed reference slices from the Wiki and StarCoder components of OLMo-Mix-1124 OLMo et al. (2024) (pretraining-distribution proxies, denoted Wiki PPL and StarCoder PPL) and on GSM8K and WMT19 Czech–English (in-mixture math and translation retention, respectively). Baselines include standard LoRA, dense down-projection fine-tuning, and the following adapter variants: PiSSA Meng et al. (2025) , LoRA-XS Bałazy et al. (2025) , TinyLoRA Morris et al. (2026) , SVF Sun et al. (2022) , VeRA Kopiczko et al. (2024) , and unpenalized NB-LoRA Wang et al. (2025) . Unless noted, adapters target all MLP down_proj layers at LoRA rank r = 896 r{=}896 ; dense down-projection fine-tuning updates the same module subset.
